Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Somalia's 2023 Data Protection Act provides for the right to an effective remedy and the DPA has an Alternative Dispute Resolution Procedure for handling complaints. The 2012 Constitution guarantees the right to privacy (Article 13). Individuals can object to data processing and seek redress through the DPA. There is no evidence of a specialized ID-specific court mechanism or judicial oversight body dedicated to digital ID. General constitutional protections and DPA complaint mechanisms apply.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: The 2023 Data Protection Act includes provisions on limitations on data sharing between the ID system and other government entities/third parties, cross-border transfer restrictions, and requirements for data controllers. The NIRA Act Law 009/2023 also references limitations on information sharing. However, the DPA Guidance and rules are still being operationalized and experts note the data sharing framework is partial—rules exist but full implementation and enforcement is ongoing.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: The National Identification and Registration Act (Law No. 009 of March 2023) is specifically dedicated to the digital ID system, establishing NIRA and its mandate, eligibility rules, biometric data requirements, and credential issuance. This is a dedicated digital ID law, not merely a general provision within broader legislation.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Somalia enacted the Data Protection Act (Law No. 005 of 2023) on March 23, 2023—the country's first comprehensive data protection law. Grounded in Article 13 of the 2012 Constitution (right to privacy), it covers rights of data subjects, obligations of controllers/processors, lawful bases for processing, breach notification, cross-border transfer restrictions, and DPIAs. The Somalia Data Protection Authority (DPA) was formally inaugurated in February 2024.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The NIRA Act (Law 009/2023) and associated regulations establish the national ID as legal proof of identity for use across public and private services. NIRA issues a credential that serves as an official, verifiable identity document. The Somalia government has mandated the ID as a legal requirement for passport applications (from September 2025) and domestic travel (from January 2026), confirming its status as legal proof of identity.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Somalia enacted the National Identification and Registration Act (Law No. 009, March 2023), establishing NIRA as the legal authority for national ID. This was accompanied by the Data Protection Act (Law No. 005, March 2023). Both laws were approved by both chambers of parliament and signed by the President. A legal framework specifically governing digital ID and data protection is clearly in place.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The National Identification and Registration Act (Law 009/2023) does not explicitly set a minimum age threshold but the system appears targeted at adults. The NIRA website and government directives reference the ID as required for passports, banking, domestic travel, and school/university enrollment, suggesting the primary eligible population is 18+. Parents register teenagers urgently for school and university admissions. No evidence of enrollment below age 10 or at birth. The minimum age of enrollment is effectively 17+.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: The NIRA Act (Law 009/2023) states that eligibility extends to 'citizens of the Federal Republic of Somalia and anyone who is a legal resident of the country, except for those who are on a short visit.' The ID policy document (2019 TOR) also states 'All residents of Somalia will be eligible for enrollment, irrespective of citizenship status.' Legal residents and refugees with legal status are eligible, but not all non-nationals (e.g., short-term visitors are excluded). This represents 'some' non-nationals being eligible.
